questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: switching languages mid-sentence is code-switching, not an error or vital. On that basis "The sentence switches from French to English mid-utterance, which is code-switching" is the supported choice.

questions.topic: A vocabulary difference between varieties

stimulus.body: Contexte du texte : The note uses 'char' in Quebec and 'voiture' in France for the same vehicle. L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Avec «Explain variety difference / Variety, not error. / A vocabulary difference between varieties» en téte, quelle option est conforme au texte ?

options.misconception: treats "A blood type" as if it followed from the evidence

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: regional varieties name the same concept differently; neither is an error. On that basis "A medication name" is the supported choice. Option B ("A spelling error") fails because it reduces variety to mistake; Option C ("Regional vocabulary variation") fails because it calls one form wrong; Option D ("A blood type") fails because it treats "A blood type" as if it followed from the evidence.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a loanword has done to French

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: Avec «New term for new concept.» en téte, quelle option est conforme au texte ?
questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the passage gives the controlling distinction: loanwords fill gaps; they do not erase the language or affect health. On that basis "Changed the patient's age" is the supported choice. Option A ("Filled a lexical gap") fails because it claims it erases French; Option C ("Erased native vocabulary") fails because it exaggerates impact; Option D ("Lowered blood pressure") fails because it confuses language with medicine.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Using a proverb in a sentence of one's own

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: « petit a petit l » Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: En appliquant «Use proverb originally / Figurative use in context. / Using a proverb in a sentence of one's own» au fragment, quelle option se justifie ?

options.text: The patient improves petit a petit

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: figurative adaptation in context shows mastery; literal reading misses it. On that basis "The proverb is ignored" is the supported choice. Option A ("The patient improves petit a petit") fails because it quotes without adapting; Option B ("A literal nest is built") fails because it reads it literally; Option C ("A medication dose") fails because it confuses proverb with prescription.
